Hive Expands European Footprint with Additional Fulfillment Centers in Poland and Spain
Hive enables even more growth potential for current and new brands with an additional state-of-the-art warehouse in Poland as well as a new one in Spain, bringing its total network to 9 Fulfillment Centers across Europe.
All Articles
Link copied!
Berlin, February 20, 2026
–  Hive, the leading end-to-end, tech-enabled operations engine powering independent brands across Europe, today announces significant upgrades to its fulfillment network. To meet surging demand and power the next phase of pan-European growth for its brands, Hive has officially opened an additional, large-scale facility in Poland (POZ2) and significantly upgraded its Spanish operations by relocating to a newly constructed, expanded facility (MAD4).
Massive Footprint in Poland
Following a period of rapid volume growth, Hive has officially opened its second Polish facility, POZ2. Located just a five-minute drive from the existing POZ1 site, the new facility ensures seamless integration with existing carrier networks while delivering a massive injection of capacity. Thanks to the location directly on the border, brands wanting to tackle the German market can benefit from the same delivery speeds as if they would send from within Germany, while experiencing a cheaper cost base due to labor market differences between the two countries.
POZ2 adds 18,884 sqm of operational space to Hive’s footprint, unlocking approximately 20,000 new pallet spaces. This expansion is not just about square footage; it is about giving brands the runway to scale without limits. By securing this additional capacity, Hive ensures that brands leveraging the cost-efficiency of Polish fulfillment have the room to grow their inventory and order volumes aggressively over the coming years.
More Growth for Spain
‍
Simultaneously, Hive is upgrading its capabilities and increasing its capacity in Southern Europe with the move to the MAD4 warehouse in Madrid. This newly constructed facility, built in 2022, represents a strategic shift toward maximum flexibility to keep up with surging demand in the region.
MAD4 offers a highly optimized and easily expandable layout designed to support even the most ambitious growth trajectories. By transitioning to this modernized space, Hive ensures that brands scaling in the Spanish market benefit from highly efficient processing flows, greater operational agility, and the physical runway needed to expand without limits.
A Network Built for Scaling
"Our mission is to empower ambitious brands to grow on their own terms. That requires an operations engine that grows faster than they do," said Oskar Ziegler, Co-Founder & CEO of Hive. "With POZ2, we are removing growing pains before they happen. With MAD4, we are upgrading our footprint in Spain. Ultimately, this expanded network provides the infrastructure to power our brands' success in 2026 and beyond."
This expansion reinforces Hive’s unique value proposition: a full operations engine unified in one App that unlocks a pan-European network of 9 fulfillment centers, ensuring <2 day delivery to 95% of Europe.
About Hive:
Hive is a tech-enabled operations engine that provides international end-to-end operations that fuels the growth of commerce brands. Powered by its innovative technology platform and a comprehensive network of fulfillment centers, Hive seamlessly manages and optimizes the entire value chain, from the supplier's factory floor through last-mile delivery to the customer's doorstep. Hive is present in Germany, France, Italy, Spain, UK, Poland, and the Netherlands.

Explore ShipBob’s Summer 2026 Releases
ShipBob Summer 2026 Release FAQs
If you’ve ever wished your fulfillment platform could think ahead of you: anticipating order exceptions, automating decisions, and giving you real-time answers without digging through dashboards, then ShipBob’s Summer 2026 Release is for you.
This isn’t a routine update; it’s a step-change in how merchants interact with their fulfillment stack. From an AI agent that takes action on your behalf to a live data protocol that connects ShipBob directly to your AI tools, this summer’s feature launches are only possible because ShipBob owns every layer of its technology.
Let’s dive deep into ShipBob’s AI releases and what they mean for your business.
AI at the foundation of ShipBob
Most fulfillment providers talk about AI. ShipBob builds with it.
ShipBob’s technology stack is built entirely in-house by more than 300 engineers, spanning:
A global fulfillment network with dozens of warehouses
Our proprietary warehouse management system (WMS)
Fulfillment and transport engines
Merchant-facing dashboards and APIs
Owning the full stack allows ShipBob to ship features that software-only platforms simply can’t build. When you want AI to analyze your inventory, reroute an order, or trigger a warehouse workflow, ShipBob’s systems are already connected end-to-end. No middleware. No lag. No limitations.
“The companies that win in this AI-native world will not be the ones with the best AI press release. They will be the ones with the strongest suite of APIs, the cleanest operational data, and the deepest action layer underpinning all of it.”
Dhruv Saxena, CEO
That action layer is exactly what’s launching this summer.
👋 Bobby: An AI agent that acts
Bobby is ShipBob’s AI agent, built directly into the merchant dashboard. Unlike AI tools that surface insights but leave execution to you, Bobby takes action on your behalf.
Ask Bobby to edit an order, resolve an exception, or build a warehouse receiving order, and it does it. Every action is logged with a full audit trail, and Bobby confirms before executing, so your team always has visibility and control.
“Before it performs any action, it actually asks you. Every single action performed through Bobby is logged, offering a clear record for your team.”
Dhruv Saxena, CEO
💡
Bobby is available now in beta directly from the ShipBob dashboard.
⚙️ Operational upgrades that you’ll feel on the floor
ShipBob’s Chief Supply Chain Officer Melissa Nick built this release around a single idea:
“At the end of the day, it only matters when you can actually feel it in your operation.”
The Summer 2026 operational updates are built around three priorities:
Faster order fulfillment:
Reduced cycle times, improved pick routing, and smarter carrier orchestration help you hit and shorten more delivery windows.
Smarter network automation:
ShipBob is deploying autonomous mobile robotics (starting in Aurora, with broader rollout in 2027). Fewer touches per order means higher throughput and fewer opportunities for error.
Easier operations:
New compliance tools turn complex retail SOPs into step-by-step automated guides for fulfillment associates, reducing errors and chargebacks.
A ShipBob employee pushes a picking cart through a warehouse aisle as she fulfills orders.
ShipBob Robotics
🛍️ Retail and B2B: Built for compliance, ready for peak
Retail and wholesale fulfillment is one of the highest-stakes areas in the supply chain,and one of the most unforgiving during peak. ShipBob’s Summer 2026 Release invests in B2B done right, including:

ShipBob Summer 2026 Release FAQs
Here are answers to some of the top questions merchants have about ShipBob’s Summer 2026 Release.
What is ShipBob’s MCP server?
ShipBob’s MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is an open connection layer that gives AI tools direct, read-and-write access to your fulfillment data. Unlike most fulfillment integrations that only let you pull information, ShipBob MCP lets your tools both retrieve and act on orders, inventory, and shipments in a single step (for example, pulling up an exception order and rerouting it without switching tabs).
What is Bobby, ShipBob’s AI agent?
Bobby is ShipBob’s embedded AI agent, built directly into the ShipBob merchant dashboard. It lets you manage your fulfillment operation using plain-language requests.
You can ask Bobby questions, and it reads your live operational data, then carries out the work: reshipping orders, creating warehouse receiving orders (WROs), updating inventory records, and more. It confirms every change before executing and logs each action so nothing happens without your knowledge.
Is Bobby available now?
Bobby is currently in beta, and the waitlist is open. Merchants can join the waitlist directly from the ShipBob dashboard at
web.shipbob.com
. ShipBob has indicated that Bobby and additional AI capabilities will continue shipping throughout 2026.
What is the ShipBob Promise?
The ShipBob Promise refers to the delivery promise ShipBob sets at checkout on behalf of its merchants. ShipBob’s Promise Engine is a component of the broader Fulfillment Engine, one of the two core AI engines that run across the ShipBob platform.
The Promise Engine uses real-time data — inventory positions, carrier performance, warehouse capacity, and network conditions — to calculate delivery dates that your operation can actually keep. It works alongside AI-driven inventory placement, order routing, carrier selection, and packaging optimization to ensure that the date shown to your customer at checkout is one ShipBob can reliably hit.
What is TrackBob?
TrackBob is ShipBob’s branded post-purchase tracking experience. It provides customers with a branded, merchant-customized tracking page that replaces generic carrier tracking links. The goal is to keep the post-purchase experience on-brand, reduce WISMO support tickets, and give customers a tracking touchpoint they actually open and engage with.

9 Best Fulfillment Companies for German E-Commerce (2026 Comparison)
Choosing the right fulfillment partner is one of the most critical decisions for e-commerce brands operating in the German market or using it as a hub for European distribution. In this guide, we compare 9 of the best fulfillment companies for German e-commerce in 2026, focusing on logistics infrastructure, technology, service quality, and pricing transparency.
Germany is the
largest e-commerce market in Europe
and one of the continent’s most important logistics hubs. With its central location, advanced transportation infrastructure, and access to major consumer markets, fulfillment operations in Germany allow e-commerce brands to reach customers quickly across the entire European Union. For many online retailers, a German fulfillment center serves not only domestic demand but also
cross-border expansion
into markets such as Austria, the Netherlands, France, and in this guide, we evaluate
9 of the best fulfillment providers serving German e-commerce businesses
, whether operating domestically or from nearby hubs, highlighting infrastructure, integrations, shipping capabilities, and service quality to help you choose the right partner.
Key Qualities of a Top Fulfillment Partner in Germany
Choosing the right fulfillment partner in Germany goes beyond warehouse space or shipping speed. Today’s e-commerce fulfillment solutions must balance
cost efficiency, fast delivery, operational flexibility, and international reach
—all while maintaining high service standards expected by German consumers.
Here are the key factors to consider when evaluating a fulfillment provider for German-based e-commerce:
1. Transparent Pricing
Fulfillment costs in Germany can be high, with warehouse labor, storage, and handling fees driving up overall expenses. The best providers offer clear, predictable pricing, so you can forecast costs and avoid unexpected charges. Cost-efficient alternatives, such as nearshoring to Poland, can deliver comparable service levels at significantly lower expenses.
2. E-commerce Platform Integration
Seamless integration with platforms like Shopify, WooCommerce, and marketplaces such as Amazon and Zalando is essential. A modern fulfillment provider automates order syncing, inventory updates, and shipping notifications, reducing errors and operational overhead.
3. Multi-Channel Support
German e-commerce businesses often sell across D2C websites, marketplaces, and B2B channels. A capable fulfillment partner manages all channels from a single platform, ensuring consistent inventory tracking and order management.
At the same time,
operating fulfillment in Germany can be expensive.
High warehouse labor costs and increasing operational expenses make it challenging for e-commerce businesses to maintain healthy margins while still delivering the fast shipping and high service standards German customers expect. As a result, many brands are now exploring more cost-efficient fulfillment strategies.
One increasingly popular solution is
nearshoring fulfillment to neighboring countries such as Poland
, where modern logistics infrastructure, lower operational costs, and strategic warehouse locations enable brands to serve Germany with
next-day delivery while reducing fulfillment expenses by up to 30–40%
. This approach allows e-commerce companies to maintain domestic-level shipping performance while improving cost efficiency and gaining easier access to fast-growing Central and Eastern European markets.
4. Inventory Management and Real-Time Visibility
Accurate stock visibility across warehouses prevents overselling and supports demand forecasting. Providers should offer real-time dashboards and reporting to help merchants make informed decisions.
5. Fast Domestic Shipping
German customers expect speedy next-day delivery. Top providers maintain efficient operations and strategically located warehouses to meet these expectations while keeping costs under control.
6. Cross-Border and European Expansion
Serving international markets efficiently is crucial for growth. Fulfillment partners with cross-border capabilities, optimized carrier partnerships, and customs support allow German merchants to reach EU markets quickly without adding complexity or cost.
7. Service Quality and Personalized Support
Dedicated account managers, SLA-based performance, and German-language support ensure smooth operations. Providers that offer flexible, tailored solutions make it easier for businesses to scale without operational bottlenecks.

How to Choose the Right Fulfilment Partner for Your E-Commerce Business

For brands seeking cost-efficient fulfillment
If you want to maintain fast delivery in Germany but reduce fulfillment expenses, consider nearshoring or software-driven solutions that optimize warehouse use and labor costs.
→ Best fits:
Omnipack, Everstox, Hive
For brands shipping across Europe

Omnipack, Byrd, Fiege, Arvato Fulfillment
For brands needing personalized support

→ Best fits:
Huboo, Omnipack, Byrd, Monta
For high-volume or multi-category ecommerce brands
If you operate a large catalog or high order volume, you need a partner with robust warehouse infrastructure, automation, and scalable processes to handle complex logistics.
→ Best fits:
Fiege Logistics, Monta, Arvato Fulfillment
For brands prioritizing tech-driven fulfillment
If you want real-time visibility, automated order routing, and multi-channel control, software-driven fulfillment platforms are ideal.
→ Best fits:
Everstox, Hive, Zenfulfillment
For brands prioritizing branded packaging & premium delivery experience
If your goal is to enhance customer experience through custom packaging, branded tracking, and smooth returns, choose fulfillment providers that support DTC branding features and personalized delivery services.
→ Best fits:
Omnipack, Monta, Zenfulfillment, Byrd
Conclusion: The Right Fulfillment Partner Can Accelerate Your Growth
Choosing the best ecommerce fulfillment partner isn’t about picking the biggest name — it’s about finding a provider that fits your goals, scale, and operational style. Whether your focus is on cost efficiency, domestic speed, European expansion, or premium branded delivery, the right fulfillment strategy can make a major difference for customer satisfaction and loyalty.
For German ecommerce businesses seeking a trusted partner with deep logistics expertise, transparent & competitive pricing, and scalable support, Omnipack is an excellent choice.
Handling both B2C and B2B orders, with seamless integration for major marketplaces like Amazon, Zalando, and Allegro, Omnipack delivers fast shipping, predictable costs, and full visibility over every step of your fulfillment operation — enabling brands to scale confidently across Germany and Europe.
